newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ICI buy-back contingent on successful offer.
newsitem.headline: ICI buy-back contingent on successful offer.

text.p: ICI Australia Ltd's buy-back of shares from parent Imperial Chemical Industries Plc would not go ahead if ICI Plc fails to sell at least 85 million other ICI Australia shares in a public offering.
ICI Australia chairman Ben Lochtenberg said on Monday the buy-back of 30 million shares, or 10 percent of the company, was contingent on the offer's success.

"If only 80 million shares are placed, or an interloper comes along (and bids for whole lot) the deal is off, if the conditions are agreed by the shareholders on Wednesday," he told a news conference.
ICI Plc owns a total 185 million shares, or 62.4 percent, of ICI Australia.
At the current market price, the stake is worth around A$2.3 billion.
ICI Australia's shares were trading at A$12.45 at 0315 GMT (1.15 p.m.) on Monday, up five cents on Friday's close in fairly light trade in the stock.
ICI Australia shareholders will vote on the buy-back at an extraordinary general meeting in Melbourne on Wednesday.

ICI Plc shareholders have also yet to vote on the overall sale, which was announced in May as part of the British group's plan to buy the specialty chemicals business of Unilever for US$8 billion in cash.
ICI Plc shareholders are due to vote on the sale on June 30.
